summary: Merge sort splits a list in half, sorts each half recursively, and merges the two sorted halves. It runs in O(n log n) time on every input.
notes: scores[:mid] and scores[mid:] make new lists, so merge_sort returns a new list and leaves the original alone.
left[i] <= right[j] uses <= so equal scores keep their original order. That makes the sort stable.
result.extend(left[i:]) copies the leftovers after one side runs out.
pitfall: Forgetting the base case if len(scores) <= 1 makes the function call itself forever and ends with RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded.
